hints: Look closely at what is actually injected: it is not pure virus, it is purified egg extract containing the viruses, so what else from the egg might still be present?
Remember that any foreign protein can act as an antigen, and that inactivated means unable to replicate, so think immune reaction versus real infection.
walkthrough:
**Spot what is in the vaccine**

The question tells you the viruses are grown in eggs and then extracted in liquid from the eggs. Even after purification, tiny amounts of egg protein remain with the viruses.

So the vaccine contains two types of foreign antigen: influenza antigens plus egg antigens.

**Recall inactivated means safe from infection**

The viruses are inactivated before use. That means they cannot replicate, cannot cause influenza, and cannot cause an infection.

Egg proteins also cannot replicate, so they cannot cause an infection either.

**Predict the real side-effect**

The immune system responds to any non-self antigen. In most people the wanted response is to the virus, but in people allergic to egg, the immune system will also respond to the egg antigens.

That unwanted immune response, like allergy, is the side-effect, so B is correct.

options.A: Auto-immune means attacking your own body tissues, but here the response is to foreign egg proteins, not self antigens.
options.B: Correct, leftover egg proteins are foreign antigens, so people with egg allergy can make an unwanted immune response to them.
options.C: Egg antigens are just proteins, they cannot replicate or spread, so they cannot cause an infection.
options.D: The influenza viruses have been inactivated, so they cannot replicate and cannot cause influenza infection.
